title: Exact trace-distance exponent for quantum privacy amplification
summary: Determine the exact asymptotic security exponent of privacy amplification against quantum side information under the operational trace-distance criterion.

formal_statement.body: Let $\rho_{XE}$ be an admissible finite-dimensional classical-quantum state and let $f_n:X^n\to Z_n$ be a hash with $n^{-1}\log|Z_n|\to R$. Writing $\rho_{Z_nE^n}^{f_n}$ for the hashed state and $\tau_{Z_n}$ for the uniform state, determine the exact optimal exponent of $$\min_{f_n}\left\|\rho_{Z_nE^n}^{f_n}-\tau_{Z_n}\otimes\rho_E^{\otimes n}\right\|_1$$ for every source-admissible $\rho_{XE}$ and extraction rate $R$. Establish matching achievability and converse formulas under the source hashing model.

scope.domain: Quantum-proof privacy amplification from i.i.d. classical-quantum sources
assumptions: The hash family and extraction-rate convention are those of the TIT source
Security is measured by trace distance from a uniform key independent of $E^n$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The 2026 preprint improves one-shot achievability and converse bounds and obtains exact second-order asymptotics, but its error-exponent upper and lower bounds still need not match. The exact trace-distance exponent remains unknown for the full source and rate domain.

progress.summary: The source explicitly asks for the corresponding quantum privacy-amplification exponent when insecurity is measured by trace distance.
A later preprint gives tighter one-shot bounds, an improved achievable exponent and a general converse, while explicitly retaining a gap between the exponent bounds.
